name: Multiple Failed Logins (Brute Force)
description: Detects multiple failed login attempts against a single user account within a short time window, indicative of password guessing or brute force attacks.
what_it_detects: Credential Access attacks targeting user accounts via repeated password attempts (brute force or password spraying variants).
benefits: Early detection of account takeover attempts. Low false positive rate when tuned with thresholds. Helps prevent successful compromises by alerting before lockouts or successes.
query: event.code:4625 and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName:* | stats count by winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, source.ip | where count >= 5

sample_results.user.name: jsmith

name: Suspicious PowerShell Encoded Command
mitre: T1059.001 - Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
description: Detects PowerShell processes launched with encoded commands, commonly used by attackers to obfuscate malicious payloads.
what_it_detects: Execution of obfuscated scripts often associated with malware droppers, initial access payloads, or post-exploitation.
benefits: Catches a very common living-off-the-land technique. High signal when combined with parent process context (e.g., from Office apps).
query: process.name:powershell.exe and process.args:(*-enc* or *-EncodedCommand* or *-e *)

name: LSASS Memory Access (Credential Dumping)
mitre: T1003.001 - OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
description: Detects processes accessing LSASS memory, a classic indicator of tools like Mimikatz used for credential dumping.
what_it_detects: Credential Access techniques aiming to extract plaintext passwords or hashes from memory.
benefits: High-fidelity detection of a core ransomware and APT technique. Immediate high-priority alert for SOC response.
query: process.name:lsass.exe and event.action:"Process Access" and process.Ext.memory_region_protection:("PAGE_READWRITE" or "PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE")

name: Ransomware Note File Creation
description: Detects creation of multiple ransomware note files (e.g., README.txt, DECRYPT.html) across directories by the same process.
what_it_detects: Ransomware encryption activity where attackers drop ransom notes after encrypting files.
benefits: Detects late-stage ransomware before or during encryption spread. Enables rapid isolation.
query: file.extension:(txt or html or hta) and file.name:(*readme* or *decrypt* or *recover* or *ransom*) and event.action:creation

name: Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
description: Detects use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware precursor to prevent recovery.
what_it_detects: Impact techniques that disable system recovery mechanisms prior to encryption.
benefits: Strong indicator of impending ransomware. Very low false positives in most environments.
query: process.name:vssadmin.exe and process.args:(delete and shadows)

name: Suspicious Service Installation
mitre: T1543.003 - Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
description: Detects creation of new Windows services, especially those pointing to unusual paths or with suspicious names.
what_it_detects: Persistence via service installation, often used by malware or attackers for long-term access.
benefits: Identifies unauthorized persistence mechanisms. Can be tuned with allowlists for legitimate admin tools.
query: event.code:7045 and winlog.event_data.ServiceName:*

name: Lateral Movement via PsExec-like Service
mitre: T1021.002 - Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
description: Detects creation of services with random 8-character executable names typical of Impacket psexec or similar tools.
what_it_detects: Lateral movement using remote service execution over SMB.
benefits: High-fidelity detection of common red team and APT lateral movement tools.
query: event.code:4697 and service.file.name:/[A-Z0-9]{8}\.exe/

name: Suspicious CloudTrail IAM Activity
description: Detects unusual IAM actions such as creating users, attaching policies, or assuming roles from unexpected sources.
what_it_detects: Privilege escalation and persistence in AWS environments via IAM manipulation.
benefits: Critical for cloud security monitoring. Helps catch account compromise early.
query: event.dataset:aws.cloudtrail and event.provider:iam.amazonaws.com and event.action:(CreateUser or AttachUserPolicy or CreateAccessKey)

name: Impossible Travel / Atypical Login Location
description: Detects successful logins from geographically distant locations in a short time frame that would be impossible for a single user.
what_it_detects: Account compromise or credential theft indicated by anomalous login locations.
benefits: Effective against stolen credentials used from different regions. Works well with identity provider logs (Okta, Entra ID, etc.).
query: event.category:authentication and event.outcome:success | stats values(source.geo.country_name) as countries by user.name | where cardinality(countries) > 1

name: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation
description: Detects creation of scheduled tasks, particularly those executing PowerShell, scripts, or from temporary directories.
what_it_detects: Persistence and execution via Windows Task Scheduler.
benefits: Common malware persistence method. Easy to baseline legitimate tasks.
query: event.code:4698 and winlog.event_data.TaskContent:(*powershell* or *cmd.exe* or *Temp*)

name: DNS Query to Suspicious TLD or Domain
description: Detects DNS queries to known malicious TLDs or high-entropy domains often used for C2.
what_it_detects: Command and Control communication via DNS tunneling or beaconing.
benefits: Catches C2 traffic that may bypass traditional firewalls. Works with DNS logs from resolvers or endpoints.
query: dns.question.name:(* .tk or * .ml or * .ga or * .cf) or dns.question.name:/[a-z0-9]{20,}\./

name: Unusual Process Parent-Child (Office Spawning Shell)
description: Detects Microsoft Office applications spawning command shells or scripting interpreters, typical of macro-based malware.
what_it_detects: Initial Access via malicious documents leading to code execution.
benefits: Classic phishing detection. High confidence when combined with email context.
query: process.parent.name:(WINWORD.EXE or EXCEL.EXE or POWERPNT.EXE) and process.name:(cmd.exe or powershell.exe or wscript.exe or cscript.exe)

name: Account Creation Followed by Privilege Escalation
mitre: T1136.001 - Create Account: Local Account / T1098
description: Correlates creation of a new user account with subsequent addition to privileged groups.
what_it_detects: Persistence and privilege escalation by creating backdoor accounts.
benefits: Sequence-based detection that is harder to evade. Strong signal of compromise.
query: sequence by host.name [event.code:4720] [event.code:4732 or event.code:4728] with maxspan=5m

name: Suspicious Outbound Connection from Unusual Process
description: Detects network connections initiated by processes that rarely make outbound connections (e.g., notepad.exe, calc.exe).
what_it_detects: C2 or data exfiltration from processes that should not be network-active.
benefits: Catches process injection or masquerading. Low noise with good baselining.
query: process.name:(notepad.exe or calc.exe or mspaint.exe) and network.direction:outbound

name: Kerberoasting Detection
mitre: T1558.003 - Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
description: Detects high volume of TGS requests for service accounts, indicative of Kerberoasting attacks.
what_it_detects: Credential Access via offline cracking of service account Kerberos tickets.
benefits: Detects a popular Active Directory attack technique used by many threat groups.
query: event.code:4769 and winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType:0x17 | stats count by winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | where count > 10

name: File Extension Anomaly (Mass Renaming)
description: Detects rapid renaming of many files to unusual extensions (e.g., .encrypted, .locked, .crypt).
what_it_detects: Ransomware file encryption activity.
benefits: Real-time detection of active encryption. Complements note file detection.
query: event.action:(rename or modification) and file.extension:(encrypted or locked or crypt or ransom) | stats count by host.name | where count > 50

name: Suspicious AWS S3 Data Exfiltration
mitre: T1537 - Transfer Data to Cloud Account
description: Detects large volume GetObject calls or CopyObject to external accounts from unusual principals.
what_it_detects: Data exfiltration from cloud storage.
benefits: Protects sensitive data in S3. Can be thresholded for volume.
query: event.dataset:aws.cloudtrail and event.action:GetObject and event.provider:s3.amazonaws.com | stats sum(aws.cloudtrail.request_parameters.bytes) by user.name

name: WMI Remote Process Creation
description: Detects remote WMI process creation, a common lateral movement technique.
what_it_detects: Lateral movement and remote execution via WMI.
benefits: Detects living-off-the-land lateral movement that avoids traditional remote tools.
query: process.name:wmiprvse.exe and process.parent.name:svchost.exe and network.direction:inbound

name: Audit Log Cleared
mitre: T1070.001 - Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
description: Detects clearing of Windows Security event logs, a common defense evasion technique.
what_it_detects: Attempts to cover tracks by deleting audit logs.
benefits: Immediate high-priority alert. Almost always malicious in production environments.
query: event.code:1102

name: Suspicious Linux Sudo or Privilege Escalation
mitre: T1548.003 - Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism: Sudo and Sudo Caching
description: Detects unusual sudo usage or privilege escalation attempts on Linux systems.
what_it_detects: Privilege escalation on Linux endpoints.
benefits: Important for mixed environments. Complements Windows coverage.
query: process.name:sudo and process.args:(*bash* or *sh* or *-i*) and not user.name:root
